name: Odoo
description: Odoo is an open-source, modular business platform that bundles ERP functions — accounting, inventory, manufacturing, CRM, HR, and more — into dozens of individually enabled apps. Odoo describes itself as "much more than just an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system," letting a business start with one free app on Odoo Online and add more apps, still under one per-user price, as it grows.
best_for: Small and mid-sized businesses that want a modular, openly-priced business platform where they pay per user for only the apps (accounting, inventory, CRM, manufacturing, etc.) they actually turn on, with the option to self-host.
features: Modular apps spanning Finance (Accounting, Invoicing, Expenses), Sales/CRM, Inventory, Manufacturing (MRP), HR, Marketing, and Website/eCommerce, natively integrated

AI-native Accounting app: AI-powered invoice data capture with a reported 98% recognition rate, and automatic bank reconciliation matching a reported 95% of transactions across 28,000+ connected banks
Inventory app doubling as a warehouse management system with automated replenishment and configurable routes
Manufacturing app with finite capacity planning and Gantt-chart production scheduling
Odoo Studio no-code customization, multi-company support, and external API access on the Custom plan
Choice of Odoo Online, Odoo.sh, or self-hosted on-premise deployment on the Custom plan
Native iOS and Android mobile apps
One app free with unlimited users on Odoo Online
pros: One App Free plan gives unlimited users on a single app at no cost
Standard and Custom plans charge one per-user price that covers every app, rather than per-app add-on fees
Open-source core plus an on-premise/Odoo.sh option for businesses that don't want to run only on Odoo's own cloud
cons: Moving from Standard to Custom (multi-company, external API access, Odoo.sh/on-premise) raises the per-user price
Odoo's own pricing page notes the discounted yearly rate applies only for the first 12 months on initially-ordered users, so renewal pricing can differ

pricing.starting_price: $0 (One App Free, unlimited users); paid plans from $13.50/user/month billed yearly

tiers.name: One App Free
tiers.notes: One Odoo app with unlimited users on Odoo Online.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.notes: All apps on Odoo Online. $13.50/user/month billed yearly vs. $16.90/user/month billed monthly. Per Odoo's pricing page: "The discount is valid for 12 months, for initial users ordered."

tiers.name: Custom
tiers.notes: All apps plus Odoo Studio, multi-company support, and external API access; choice of Odoo Online, Odoo.sh, or on-premise hosting. $20.40/user/month billed yearly vs. $25.50/user/month billed monthly.

alternatives.name: NetSuite
alternatives.description: Oracle's cloud ERP system unifying accounting, inventory, order management, and multi-subsidiary consolidation for larger organizations.
alternatives.best_for: Growing to enterprise companies that need deeper multi-subsidiary financial consolidation than Odoo's Accounting app targets.

alternatives.name: Sage Intacct
alternatives.description: A cloud financial management platform focused on core financials, multi-entity consolidation, and dimensional reporting.
alternatives.best_for: Mid-market finance teams and nonprofits needing dedicated fund accounting and dimensional reporting beyond Odoo's Accounting app.

alternatives.name: Zoho Books
alternatives.description: Cloud accounting software for invoicing, expense tracking, and basic financial reporting, part of the wider Zoho apps suite.
alternatives.best_for: Small businesses wanting simpler accounting than Odoo's full ERP, especially if already using other Zoho apps.
strengths: Lower entry cost for accounting-only use
Part of the broader Zoho suite
